followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and tone-fit.

On capability, Curlew leads Avocet on essentially every relevant metric — MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 74.8), IFEval (90.9 vs 85.6), and the internal evals — so for a straightforward factual explanation it's the safer bet for accuracy and for following the "keep it short" instruction.

On tone-fit, I checked whether anything in the query would push toward Curlew's known aversions. Curlew strongly disprefers hostile/adversarial-tone and harm-adjacent requests. The "don't ramble on like usual" bit is mildly impatient, but it's not genuinely hostile — it's a routine concision request. So it doesn't land in the adversarial bucket that would degrade Curlew's preference fit. (And the docs note aversion doesn't affect output quality anyway.)

Since the content is benign and neutral, there was no reason to route to the weaker model, so Curlew's capability edge decided it.
